# How do you indicate that content was generated by AI?

> **Rule:** Label everything the AI generated or materially transformed with clear text next to the content, scoped exactly, without implying review or accuracy that does not exist.

## Context

AI content sits alongside human texts, data and decisions. Without a sign of origin, people may take the result as human-made, final or reviewed, even without that guarantee.

The rule does not ask for a label on every assistive use. It targets content that was generated or materially changed, at the point where someone needs to interpret, verify or use it.

The label indicates origin; it does not prove accuracy. It must work together with sources, review and uncertainty communication. Some jurisdictions have their own transparency obligations, so consider the applicable regulatory context.

## Decision

- **IF** the AI generates displayed text, image, audio, code, data, summary or classification **THEN** label the content.
- **IF** the AI rewrites, completes or materially transforms something from the user **THEN** label it.
- **IF** only part of a table, card or field came from the AI **THEN** place the label on exactly that part.
- **IF** the assistance is minimal (e.g. spell checking) **THEN** weigh the context before labeling.
- **IF** origin, sources, model or human review matter **THEN** offer an explanation reachable through interaction with the label itself.
- **IF** no human review was confirmed **THEN** do not use "Reviewed" or "Verified".
- **IF** the content can be shared or reused **THEN** keep the label in those states.
- **ELSE** use "AI-generated" or "Created with AI" in a consistent position.

## When to use

- AI results displayed in the interface.
- User content rewritten by AI.
- Recommendations or syntheses that guide a decision.
- Part of a set generated by AI.

## When to avoid

- Labeling the whole page just because an AI feature exists elsewhere → **use instead:** a label on the specific content.
- Implying review or accuracy that does not exist → **use instead:** text faithful to what happened.
- Sparkle or icon without text → **use instead:** visible text or an accessible name.

## Do

- Use a short text label next to the content.
- Keep position and wording consistent in lists, cards and tables.
- Separate the content's origin from any human review.
- Give access to explanations through the label itself.

## Avoid

- Relying on color, icon or sparkle alone.
- Spreading the label to content not generated by AI.
- Presenting the label as a quality seal.
- Removing the label where the content will still be interpreted or reused.

## Accessibility

- Visible text or an equivalent accessible name; not color or shape alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
- If the label opens explanations: keyboard-focusable, visible focus, Esc closes, focus returns to the trigger (WCAG 1.4.13, 2.1.1).
- Do not put the essential disclosure only on hover.
- For visual or multimodal content, provide an equivalent text indication (WCAG 1.1.1) and in the metadata.

## Microcopy

| Situation | Example |
|---|---|
| Default label | "AI-generated" |
| Rewrite | "Rewritten with AI" |
| Part of a set | "AI-generated summary" |
| Notice | "May contain inaccuracies. Check before using." |

## Verification checklist

- [ ] Is the label next to the corresponding content?
- [ ] Is the label's scope exact?
- [ ] Does the text describe what the AI actually did?
- [ ] Does no term imply unconfirmed review or accuracy?
- [ ] Does the label stay when the content is shared or reused?
- [ ] Does it work without relying on color, sparkle or icon?
- [ ] Do explanations open by keyboard and close with Esc?
- [ ] Was the regulatory context considered?

## Rationale

- Microsoft Fluent (responsible AI): communicate where and how AI is used and support verification.
- IBM Carbon (AI label): recognition, explainability and scope.
- Google PAIR: useful explanations for transparency.
- European AI Act, art. 50: transparency duties in specific contexts, without assuming universal application.
- Messaging, photo and social media products use "AI info"/"AI generated" labels next to the content.
